seoDescription: Learn how to build a complete admin dashboard in Laravel using the Filament package: install Filament with Composer, create admin users, generate resources for models, configure table columns and forms, handle file uploads and storage linking, and secure admin access with authentication or middleware. The tutorial demonstrates creating a Customer model, migrations, Filament resources, image fields, and common UI adjustments with links to Filament documentation for advanced features.

chapters.description: Generate the Customer Filament resource, configure table columns to display data, add form fields for name and email, and test create/edit actions.

chapters.title: Actions: Edit, Delete, and Adding Image Upload Field
chapters.description: Demonstrate editing and deleting customer records, add a file upload field, and configure storage and table display for images.

summary:
## Key Concepts

- **Filament**: a Laravel admin package that scaffolds resources, forms, tables, and actions for models to build admin dashboards quickly.

- **Installation & setup**
  - Install via Composer: composer require filament/filament
  - Create an admin user: php artisan make:filament-user
  - Run migrations: php artisan migrate

- **Resources & scaffolding**
  - Generate Filament resources: php artisan make:filament-resource ResourceName
  - Resource files live in app/Filament/Resources/ResourceNameResource.php
  - Configure **table columns** (TextColumn::make(...)) and **form schema** (TextInput::make(...), FileUpload::make(...)) inside the resource.

- **Models & migrations**
  - Create model with migration: php artisan make:model Customer -m
  - Define columns in migration (name, email, image) and run php artisan migrate
  - Add **protected $fillable** in the model for fields you will create/update via Filament.

- **Actions & CRUD**
  - Filament auto-generates Create and Edit UIs after adding form schema.
  - Add DeleteAction in the resource table actions to enable record deletion.

- **File uploads & storage**
  - Use FileUpload component and import the component at the top of the resource file.
  - Uploaded files are stored in storage/app/public; run php artisan storage:link to expose them via public/storage.
  - Ensure APP_URL in .env matches the development URL and remove trailing slashes so images render correctly.

- **Customization & extras**
  - Filament supports filters, table builder, form builder, notifications, and UI customization via documentation.
  - Use CSS/config options to adjust image size, shape, and table appearance.

> [!TIP]
> Copy table column and form component examples from the Filament "Getting Started" docs to speed up configuration.

> [!NOTE]
> Always add the model's **$fillable** fields; otherwise Filament won't be able to persist form data.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> When adding images, create the storage symlink (php artisan storage:link) and ensure APP_URL is correct so uploaded files are publicly accessible.

## Takeaways

- Filament dramatically reduces boilerplate for admin panels by generating resources and UI elements.
- Proper model setup (fillable) and Laravel storage/public linking are required for file uploads to work.
- Authentication and middleware should be applied when using an existing users table to restrict admin access.
